title: <An English title in one form only: the official product name, a colon, and a general subject named at the charter's own level of generality, as a standing page of a real company's policy manual would be titled. Never a question, never an internal-procedure label, never the particular combination of circumstances a task presents, never wording that signals a dependency, a sequence or a remedy, and never words coined for retrieval.>
content:
<English markdown, in the register of a formal policy manual, one topic per document. The KB and the structured source are in strict bijection at the level of normative semantic atoms: every rule in the source must have exactly one home in the prose, and every calculation, eligibility, authorisation, evidence requirement, step, ordering, question, confirmation, wait, review, notification, exception handling and business effect in the prose must trace back to exactly one structured source locator. Never add a policy the source does not contain in order to enrich the content, make it feel realistic, or make it safer; in particular, never turn a tool parameter into a 'must ask / must confirm' step, and never add delivery dates, customer confirmations, read-backs, post-action reviews, duplicate guards, corrections, approvals, waits or handoff steps. When the source material is thin, a short document or an omitted section with no source is allowed; there is no minimum word count or average length.

What the solver is meant to work out (a dependency between problems, the order of actions across problems, the course of a workflow, the way a situation is resolved) is carried only by entailment from the definitions and principles the documents state, and is never written out: no entry condition, no gating clause that makes one problem wait on another, no precedence label, no before / first / only-after directive about another problem's action, no ordered steps or sequence of tool names, no contrast between a wrong and a correct reading, no named mistake. For a prerequisite, the blocked side states in abstract terms what its governed result is and what it may never rest on; the depended-on side states its own rule independently, in different words, using the plain business terms the records show; neither mentions the other, and the dependency follows only when a reader applies both to the facts, at exactly the source's strength. Every sentence is paraphrased in the document's own words: nothing is copied from the charter and no phrasing recurs across documents. Identifiers the solver must reproduce exactly (tool names, their parameter names and enum values, fixed phrases a tool accepts, the product's official display name) stay exact, in backticks when inside prose.

Use `##` sections only where the source semantics support them (scope of application / basis of decision / exceptions and non-application / handling notes), state rules as clauses, and use a table for per-tier values; write complete clause-style sentences with formal terms of address and no colloquialism. Express every calculation relationship in words (multiplied by / less / total / the higher of), and never use arithmetic symbols, but never compress the base the source rule pins down, its ordering/grouping, its cap/floor, or the point at which it rounds; state a calculation as a definition of the resulting quantity, precise enough that only one reading is natural, never as a procedure or a warning against a wrong reading. The document must make plain early on which product category it governs (naming it verbatim with the official display_name from the charter) and its general subject, without a scenario-style opening and without an opening shared with other documents. There must be no table names, field names, event types, parameter keys, policy ids, DSL, row ids, or implementation-facing phrasing such as 'writes to / lands in the table / field'; the only code-shaped tokens allowed are tool names, and, in the parameter section of that tool's own invocation document, that tool's parameter names and enum values. Take one of the following shapes according to role:

[facet document (role=facet)] One facet that genuinely exists in the source, across all tiers: render only the applicable basis from the source and a parameter table covering every tier. The quantitative keys this document carries are declared in meta.carries (no more than six keys). Write the exceptions or handling sections only where the source actually has them.

[policy document (role=policy)] The complete equivalent text of one base policy: the rule and all of its eligibility conditions, including the applicable events, the authority boundary between system records and customer statements, and the correlation to the business object of this transaction. Where the source has a time gate, keep the business event the clock starts from, the verifiable record, the day/month counting algorithm for anchor plus duration, the direction of comparison, the equality boundary, and the source's prescribed handling when it is not met; never add negative space, communication actions or exception flows the source does not have.

[hub document (role=hub)] State the entry point to the policy only as far as the trigger, subject, rule and target tool of that extended policy support, with the applicable situation stated generally; factor names, counts, component inventories, calculation steps, cross-category hints, fragment navigation and reading-completion cues are all forbidden. It states nothing about another problem except, where it is a prerequisite's principle home, an abstract principle about its own governed result, never an entry condition. Do not add reassuring steps such as confirmation, dates, read-backs or reviews. meta must not contain factors/covers, and carries must be empty. When the tool is exclusive to this policy, the hub doubles as the invocation document and sets meta.tool; describe each parameter only as far as task_tools can prove (meaning, format, enum and return), and never turn the existence of a parameter into a policy precondition. When the tool is shared, do not set meta.tool, and do not list parameters or navigate to the tool document.

[factor, an independent policy fragment (role=factor)] Carries exactly one independent business rule that can be located in the structured source, including the applicable conditions, the way it takes effect, its quantitative basis and its non-application boundary as the source already has them. The prose never calls itself a factor / satellite / the Nth item, and never mentions the hub, the other fragments, the total fragment count or a reading order. meta.factor is a hidden short name; meta.covers claims the source compute bindings. Handling hints and exceptions with no source are not written.

[meta_rule document (role=meta_rule)] Losslessly states the combination rule the source rule/compute already fixes, preserving the objects it acts on, the original or intermediate base, the ordering/grouping, the cap/floor and the point at which it rounds, as an exact definition of the combined result; it does not re-choose the algorithm, does not list all the components, does not navigate to the factors, and does not contrast a wrong reading with a correct one. meta.covers claims the composite source binding this document implements.

[tool document (role=tool)] For a non-calculating tool, or a calculating tool shared by at least two extended policies. All four sections come only from task_tools.py: the situation of use and the business effect the function can prove, described at the level of the capability rather than the circumstances of a task; how it is invoked and its owner, in this document's own words; the parameter names, the meanings the source can prove, the formats and the full enum sets; and the successful return and explicit errors the source can prove. The existence of a parameter creates no asking or confirmation step; where the source defines no error, review, correction or duplicate-guard behaviour, none may be added.

[workflow document (role=sop)] Carries the yaml workflow's situation, parts, owners, dataflow and order_rationale in principle form, never as a runbook: the class of situation it governs, stated generally; what each part achieves, in business language; who performs each kind of part (owner=user only as something the customer does themselves, never automatically a customer confirmation); and why one part's outcome is what another relies on, so that the order follows from the reasons. No numbered or ordered steps, no step or role table, no process arrows, no tool names, no before/after entry condition, no reordering counter-example, and no description of the particular combination of circumstances a task presents. Do not add preparation, confirmation, waiting, receipt verification, closing review or exception handling unless the workflow source explicitly contains it.

No document states when to hand off to a human without a structured source for it. Length is determined by how much real information the single source can carry; usually no more than about 2600 characters, though it may exceed that where precisely covering the source genuinely requires it. Padding the length with tables of contents, repeated definitions, navigation, confirmation/review or invented exception flows is forbidden.>

meta.source: <relative path of the source yaml, e.g. env/<scenario>/tasks/<difficulty>/<product>.extended.yaml or env/<scenario>/blueprint/products/<product>.yaml>
meta.role: <hub | factor | meta_rule | facet | policy | tool | sop>
meta.policy_id: <when role is one of {hub,factor,meta_rule}: the id of the extended policy it belongs to; when role=policy: the base policy id; omitted otherwise>
meta.workflow: <when role=sop: the workflow id; omitted otherwise>
meta.tool: <when role is one of {hub,tool}: the name of the task tool for which this document is the invocation document; omitted otherwise>
meta.factor: <when role=factor: a hidden short name used only by the gate to tell apart independent fragments of the same policy; unique within one policy_id, and never transcribed into the hub; omitted otherwise>
covers: <required when role is one of {factor,meta_rule}: the names of the source extended policy compute bindings this document implements. A factor may leave it empty when it carries a constant / eligibility / cross-category branch with no binding of its own; a meta_rule needs at least one. Every binding is claimed by exactly one document across the whole corpus; omitted for other roles; strictly forbidden on a hub.>
carries: <the quantitative basis keys this document carries. A hub must be empty; a factor no more than two; a facet no more than six; each key appears exactly once across the whole corpus.>
